dedupe_keys.name: sand motor zandmotor mega nourishment on the delfland coast

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Sand Motor, a building-with-nature mega-nourishment placed on the Delfland coast of South Holland, the Netherlands, between March and November 2011 as a pilot. A single deposit of sand, equivalent to about 20 years of regular nourishment, formed a hook-shaped peninsula from which waves, currents and wind spread sand along the coast, protecting low-lying land from erosion and sea level rise while creating new habitat and recreation space. The Netherlands has a 350 km coastline with nine million coastal residents, and a regional sea level rise of 0.65 to 1.3 m is projected by 2100. It cost 70 million euros, funded by the Province of South Holland and Rijkswaterstaat, and has been monitored closely; a five-year evaluation in 2016 found the coastline near the Sand Motor had moved seaward. The page, published in 2019 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the Sand Motor and Deltares project pages. Caveats: the final assessment expected in 2021 is not reported on the page, and benefits concentrate near the deposit. It illustrates nature-based coastal flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation of sea defences; related records are the Building with Nature Indonesia (Demak) and Kruibeke Bazel Rupelmonde case studies and the Global Mangrove Watch.
name: Sand Motor (Zandmotor) mega-nourishment on the Delfland coast
outcomes: Five years after construction the coastline at and next to the Sand Motor had moved seaward, supporting coastal protection while adding habitat and recreation space.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study based on the Sand Motor website, Deltares, Rijkswaterstaat and the Province of South Holland
